md5.identity: Native 32-bit Remcos agent, unrelated to an MD5 utility
md5.configuration: RCDATA SETTINGS RVA 0x1c9a4, 418 bytes: one-byte key length 149, then RC4 key, then ciphertext; decrypted separator is 0x1e
execution_paths: 0x409146 main -> 0x409c5e -> 0x40a0e9 FindResource/LoadResource/LockResource -> 0x403198 RC4 initialization -> 0x40329b stream transform -> split settings at 0x411fcc.
Config field 15 is ASCII 1; main 0x4098b0 sets keylogging mode, reaches 0x409a85 -> 0x4051dc. Hook thread 0x405332 installs WH_KEYBOARD_LL and pumps messages.
Clipboard reads at 0x406c29 and 0x40e3e5; audio waveInOpen/Start at 0x401459/0x401472 and 0x4018bd/0x40192e.

0x4023d2 receives C2 socket data, accumulates bytes and hands them to 0x4024a0 for packet/callback dispatch. File-transfer and command handlers coexist with keyboard, clipboard, screen and microphone capture.

0x40f2ef checks MZ/PE, creates suspended process, reads PEB image base from context EBX+8, optionally unmaps image, allocates remote executable memory, writes headers/sections and PEB, sets thread context and resumes.

0x407e01 builds Run/Explorer Policies Run and Winlogon Shell/Userinit values. Userinit branch 0x407f2b concatenates a path after userinit.exe comma prefix, passes Userinit/HKLM/Winlogon to 0x40ba71, which calls RegCreateKeyW and RegSetValueExW.
0x4032e9 writes the mscfile open command and launches Event Viewer; 0x40a4c8 launches hidden cmd/reg EnableLUA=0 command. Both are config-gated.
0x407136 targets Chrome Login Data and deletes it. Existing browser-store deletion and surveillance detections are preserved.
md5.configuration_limits: Offline keylogging is configured. Anti-analysis, UAC bypass and EnableLUA-disable options checked at indices 28/29/31/32/33/34, 46 and 39 are zero. Persistence writer is a capability, not a claim that this configuration enabled Userinit modification. No runtime connection success or deployment authorization is known.
md5.verdict_reason: Configured covert keylogging with a preselected controller plus invasive RAT tasking, capture and hollowing capabilities outweigh a possible authorized remote-administration use; no consent/deployment context was supplied.

poll.execution: Backward CHECK_COMMAND loop downloads cmd.txt with curl; SET /P loads its first line; %command% executes it and redirects stdout to output.txt; waits ten seconds and repeats.
poll.limitations: POST sends output=!command!, never reads output.txt, and does not enable delayed expansion. It may send a literal !command! or the command text if expansion was inherited. No output exfiltration claim is made. The .example endpoint is a documentation placeholder; live deployment and instructional intent are unknown.
poll.verdict_reason: Unvalidated remote command execution repeats without a user-selected command, authorization check or consent path; likely a backdoor/demo of a backdoor.
poll.coverage_goal: One distinct hostile objective is supported. Checked for staging, persistence, concealment, cleanup, credential theft and actual output return: absent from the bytes. Three to five distinct hostile traits would invent or duplicate behavior. Bounded source matcher covers this simple unquoted file form; general CMD expansion is not modeled.

npm.identity: @open-xamu-co/ui-common-helpers 3.1.0, published UI/form/i18n helpers; bundled SweetAlert2 identifies itself as 11.17.2
npm.reachability: package main/module exports point to dist/index.js/index.mjs. These eagerly require/import swal chunks. The UMD factory is immediately invoked by the swal chunk, so the regional code runs on module load without calling a dialog helper. No install hook is involved.
npm.payload: If window exists, browser language matches /^ru\b/, and location.host ends in .ru/.su/.by/.xn--p1ai, store first visit in localStorage. More than three days later, schedule pointerEvents=none after 500ms, append looping audio with a remote MP3 URL, then attempt play after 2500ms and discard rejection.
npm.second_review: Traced both CJS and ESM copies and all listed entry points. Normal DOM, clipboard sharing, image/FileReader, i18n and form paths fit advertised helpers. Dynamic Function use is Lodash template compilation or SweetAlert template parameters; Unicode-region decoding can include unchanged surrounding Function text. No additional credential theft, OS execution or data exfiltration was established.
npm.verdict_reason: Undisclosed user input sabotage and unsolicited remote audio are reachable in normal browser imports and are unrelated to helper functionality; no extension-origin or text-only execution restriction is present.
npm.coverage_goal: Archive retains three existing hostile findings. Each swal member has one compound sabotage finding; splitting its gates, input blocking and audio into additional hostile duplicates would not add an independent attack. No evidence supports further hostile objectives.
npm.runtime_limits: The isolated trace confirms control flow with stubs only. Actual browser storage access, page origin, autoplay policy, audio availability and consumer deployment determine runtime effects.

trait_corrections: Batch read/variable-command atoms moved from C2 objectives to notable file-read and shell-command capabilities. Ordinary curl file output remains covered by existing canonical notable download traits. Label-dependent component replaced by bound backward-label flow.

The hostile batch composite moved to remote-command/http-poll. Inline YARA checks equality of downloaded and read filenames, read and executed variable names, and backward jump target; rejects intervening read-to-execution reassignment.
Native Userinit matcher binds executable prefix, Userinit value and Winlogon key operands to C++ argument construction in .text. Family composite adds Remcos identity and registry-write API chain.

Decoded Function text moved unchanged to source-syntax metadata. Exact consumers updated; image-stego consumer retains it explicitly. Three broad concealment consumers intentionally no longer accept neutral decoded syntax as concealment.

Two URLMon profiles and one WinInet profile renamed to API co-occurrence claims, with every exact consumer updated and matching/severity preserved. Removed unsupported T1027 annotations from URLMon profiles.
Regional sabotage descriptions no longer assert an exact three-day threshold when matchers accept general elapsed-day comparisons.
